answers.label: The act of a being in potency insofar as it is in potency: the gradual acquiring of a form
An affection of the natural body by which it acquires one place after another
The transfer of a body from the neighbourhood of the bodies that immediately touch it into the neighbourhood of others

questions.wording: Which changes are motions in the proper sense?

answers.label: Change in quantity, quality and place; coming to be and passing away are instantaneous and not motions
Only change of place; the other changes are not motion, or belong elsewhere

questions.wording: Is whatever is moved moved by something other than itself?
names: la: omne quod movetur ab alio movetur

answers.label: Yes: nothing moves itself as a whole; animals move one part by another, heavy bodies have their motion from what generated them
No: a body moved naturally, from an internal principle, moves itself; only violent motion is from another

questions.wording: What is the first cause of motion in the world?

answers.label: God, the first mover

questions.wording: Does the same quantity of motion remain in the world?

answers.label: Yes: God conserves the quantity he gave at the creation; what one body loses another gains
No

questions.wording: Are some motions in nature violent, that is, against the inclination of the body moved?

answers.label: Yes: violent motion has an outside principle the body does not cooperate with, as a stone thrown upward
No: every motion is as natural to bodies as rest; violence refers only to a will

questions.wording: What is contrary to a motion?

answers.label: Rest alone; one motion is not contrary to another, though one direction may be contrary to another
A motion between opposite terms, as between contrary qualities or opposite places

questions.wording: Along what line does a moving body tend to go of itself?

answers.label: A straight line only; a body moves in a curve only when other bodies force it, and so tends away from the centre
Straight, to or from the centre of the world, for the elements; circular for the stars

questions.wording: Is the direction in which a body moves something distinct from its motion?

answers.label: Yes: the determination can change or be taken away while the quantity of motion stays the same
No

questions.wording: Does a body come to rest for a moment at the point where it rebounds?
names: fr: moment de repos au point de reflexion

answers.label: Yes
No: the reflected motion is the continuation of the direct one

questions.wording: Is the angle of reflection equal to the angle of incidence?

answers.label: Equal
Equal when the body keeps its speed; smaller or greater when the striking changes its speed

questions.wording: Why does a body or a ray change its path when it passes obliquely from one medium into another?

answers.label: The new medium resists more or less, which changes the part of the determination across the surface and not the part along it

collision.label: A moving body that pushes another loses as much motion as it gives, so that the two go on together at one speed as one mass; a body it cannot shake it reflects at its own speed

motion-transfer.label: No body moves another; when bodies meet, God, the universal cause, applies his moving force to the other body

fall-cause.label: The heavy body has its downward motion from what generated it, as a property following its nature

fall-acceleration.label: The air resists at the start and then, set moving by the falling body, helps it on

first-law-grounds.label: Nothing tends of itself to its own destruction, and rest is contrary to motion

notes: Twelve new questions on motion (motion-definition with child motion-kinds; mover-other; first-mover with child motion-conserved; violent-motion; motion-contrary; motion-line; determination; reflection-rest) and on reflection and refraction (reflection-angle, refraction-cause, under light and fire so the light entries can reuse them). The claims rest on matter-form (1675-matter-form-013, -017) and place-void-time (1675-place-void-time-001, -005, -006) for the Cartesians' extension, plenum and impenetrability. Rohault and Le Grand's reflection and refraction follow Descartes' Dioptrique closely, down to the cannon balls skipping in sea fights; Le Grand names Descartes, Rohault does not. Le Grand's fourth rule of impact is printed with the letters A and E interchanged (p. 254).
